title: Report writing
examples: What is the difference between a report and an essay?
How do I make sure my report sounds professional?
What should I include in the introduction of a report?

explain.say: A report needs clear headings to guide the reader.
Headings help organize your ideas into clear sections.
The objective tone means you write facts, not feelings.
When writing objectively, you avoid using personal opinions.
For a real-life example, write a report on a school trip.
A common mistake is mixing personal feelings with facts.

faq.q: Should I use fancy vocabulary in my report?
faq.a: No, you should use clear and straightforward language. Fancy words can sometimes confuse your reader.
asks: Is simple language okay for reports?

faq.q: How do I know what headings to use?
faq.a: Think about the main parts of your topic. Each main part can become a heading for your report.
asks: Should I use too many headings?

faq.q: What is the difference between objective and subjective?
faq.a: Objective means reporting what is true, like facts. Subjective means including your personal feelings or opinions.
asks: Can I use 'I think' in a report?

faq.q: Do I need an introduction section?
faq.a: Yes, an introduction tells the reader what the report is about. It sets the purpose for the rest of the writing.
asks: What is the first paragraph supposed to do?

faq.q: Can I use numbers and statistics in my report?
faq.a: Yes, using numbers and statistics makes your report sound very factual and strong. These are great pieces of evidence.

facts: A report must have clear headings to guide the reader.
An objective tone means reporting facts without personal feelings.
The introduction section states the report's purpose.
Headings help break the report into manageable sections.

quiz.say: Which of these statements is purely objective?
quiz.show: A) The film was breathtakingly beautiful.

options.show: I felt the film was too long.
options.say: I felt the film was too long.

options.show: It was a very good movie.
options.say: It was a very good movie.

options.show: The film ran for ninety minutes.
options.say: The film ran for ninety minutes.

quiz.why: This statement only gives verifiable information about the film's length.

wrong.0: This uses first-person pronouns and personal feeling.
wrong.1: This uses vague positive language instead of facts.
wrong.3: This uses strong adjectives that show personal feeling.

quiz.say: If you write a report on local wildlife, what should one heading be?
quiz.why: This heading groups factual information about where animals live and what they eat.

wrong.0: This sounds like an opinion, not a factual report section.
wrong.1: This focuses on the writer's experience rather than the facts.
wrong.2: This is too informal and uses exclamation marks.

quiz.say: When writing about a historical event, which tone is best?
quiz.why: A neutral tone ensures you present the known facts without bias.

wrong.0: This is too subjective and sounds like storytelling.
wrong.1: This focuses too much on the writer's personal thoughts.
wrong.3: This shows too much emotion and is not objective.
